Before claiming "this is impossible," remember: humans have accidentally done smart things before.

Not often. But occasionally, when properly motivated by either fear or greed (usually both), the species stumbles into competence.

Here is proof society has done every single part of this plan already. It just hasn't combined them yet, like someone who owns all the ingredients for bread but keeps eating them separately.

## Humans Doing Smart Things (Accidentally): A Collection

### That Time Humans Banned Landmines (Yes, Really)

**What happened:** NGOs decided landmines were bad actually. They convinced [160 nations to sign a treaty banning them](../references.qmd#icbl-ottawa-treaty) in 1997. Major military powers initially opposed it. The NGOs won anyway.

**Why this matters:** This proves citizen movements can create binding international law even when governments don't want to. If humans can globally ban a weapon because "it's mean," they can definitely get nations to redirect 1% of the murder budget to the not-murder budget.

### War Bonds: That Time The Public Funded WW2

**What happened:** Governments needed money to fight Nazis. They sold "war bonds" - basically IOUs that paid interest - directly to regular people. The U.S. raised [$185 billion](../references.qmd#wwii-war-bonds) (trillions in today's papers).

**Why this matters:** Previous generations gave the government money to stop Hitler and got 4% returns. This plan offers {{< var victory_bond_annual_return_pct >}} returns to stop cancer. [VICTORY Incentive Alignment Bonds](../economics/victory-bonds-academic.qmd) are the same thing except with better ROI and fewer Nazis (hopefully zero Nazis).

The formula worked: mix moral incentives (patriotism) with financial self-interest (interest payments). This just applies it to a different war - the one against mortality.

### The Global Fund (Proof That New Health Institutions Can Exist)

**What happened:** In 2002, the world created a [new organization](../references.qmd#global-fund) to pool billions for fighting AIDS, TB, and malaria. It bypassed traditional bureaucracies and just... worked.

**Why this matters:** A network of decentralized institutes of health ([DIH](../solution/dih-academic.qmd)) isn't fantasy. It is the Global Fund but bigger and for all diseases. If humans can create new health institutions for three diseases, they can create one for all of them. It is just multiplication.

### Post-WW2: That Time America Accidentally Discovered Peace Is Profitable

**What happened:** 1945: US military spending was [37% of GDP](../references.qmd#us-post-wwii-military-spending-cut) (they were very serious about the war thing). 1948: Cut to 7%. That's a 30 percentage point drop - not 1%, THIRTY.

**The results:** The greatest economic boom in human history:
  - GDP growth: [8% yearly for a decade](../references.qmd#us-post-wwii-gdp-growth-8-pct) (vs normal 2-3%)
  - [Home ownership doubled](../references.qmd#us-post-wwii-home-ownership-doubled) (middle class explosion)
  - GI Bill created modern knowledge economy
  - Built the interstate highway system

**Why this matters:** The treaty asks for 1%. America did 30% and got rich. This is like asking someone who lost 100 pounds if they can spare 3 pounds. The answer is obviously yes, and they will probably feel better.

### The 1990s: When the Berlin Wall Fell and Wallets Exploded

**What happened:** Cold War ended. Military spending dropped from 6% of GDP to 3%. That's $300B redirected from aiming missiles at Russia to literally anything else.

**The results:** The 1990s economic boom everyone remembers fondly:
  - Internet became commercial (freed resources)
  - First budget surplus in 30 years
  - Unemployment: 3.9% (lowest in a generation)
  - Productivity: +2.5% yearly (double the normal rate)

**Why this matters:** The pattern isn't subtle. Every time humans stop spending money on murder, prosperity appears like magic. It is not magic. It is arithmetic.

### Switzerland: 200 Years of Not Shooting Anyone = Being Very Rich

**What they have:** Mountains, cows, and a complete lack of natural resources. They are surrounded by countries that kept starting world wars. They have been neutral since 1815.

**What they spend on military:** 0.7% of GDP (purely defensive - they aren't invading anyone with those Alps)

#### The results

  - $93K GDP per capita (vs US $76K)
  - Universal healthcare, excellent quality, 12% of GDP (vs US 18%)
  - Life expectancy: 84 years (vs US 79)
  - Last invaded: Never (Napoleon tried in 1798, didn't go well for him)

**Why this matters:** Peace dividends compound over centuries. Switzerland proves nations don't need oil, colonies, or weapons to get rich. They just need to not waste money on awful things. They have been doing this for 200 years. This plan asks for a 1% start.

## When Good Intentions Met Reality (And Lost)

Failures teach more than successes. Here is every mistake past movements made, so this plan does not repeat them.

### Eisenhower's Warning: A 5-Star General Tried to Tell The Public

In 1961, President Dwight D. Eisenhower - former 5-star general, Supreme Allied Commander, the guy who beat the Nazis - used his farewell address to warn the public about something terrifying:

**The warning:** "We must guard against the military-industrial complex."

**The reality check:** "Every gun made, every warship launched, every rocket fired signifies theft from those who hunger."

**The prophecy:** He predicted the permanent war economy humans currently live in, where military spending becomes self-perpetuating regardless of whether anyone is actually threatening the nation.

**Why this matters:** Eisenhower understood one cannot dismantle the system. One has to give it something more profitable to build instead. He was right. Nobody listened. Now this plan attempts his solution: redirect the resources.

### The Nuclear Freeze Movement: Millions of People, Zero Results

**What happened:** In the 1980s, a [massive global movement](../references.qmd#nuclear-disarmament-movement-freeze) tried to freeze nuclear weapons production. Millions of protesters. Enormous popular support. Good vibes everywhere.

**The result:** Failed completely. Nuclear arsenals kept growing.

**Why it failed:** Good intentions cannot defeat money. The military-industrial complex has more money than God, and protesters have signs. This is why a 1% treaty doesn't ask nicely - it bribes everyone into submission. It is not fighting greed, it is redirecting it.

**The lesson:** Make peace more profitable than war, or peace loses. Every time.

### Occupy Wall Street: When "Diffuse Anger" Isn't a Strategy

**What happened:** In 2011, thousands [occupied parks](../references.qmd#occupy-wall-street) to protest economic inequality. They changed the conversation! They raised awareness! They accomplished nothing permanent!

**Why it failed:** No specific demand. Just diffuse anger at "the system." The energy dissipated because nobody knew what success looked like.

**Why this matters:** This plan has ONE demand: ratify a [1% treaty](../solution/1-percent-treaty-academic.qmd). That's it. Not "fix inequality" or "be better." One specific, achievable, measurable goal. A network of decentralized institutes of health (DIH), a decentralized framework for drug assessment ([dFDA](../solution/dfda-academic.qmd)), and the cures are all downstream of that single objective.

When people ask for everything, they get nothing. When people ask for 1%, they might get it.

## On How Rich People Made Money Doing Crazy Things (And Why That Matters)

To make this work, the plan needs investment terms that don't sound insane to people with money. Fortunately, history is full of rich people doing riskier things for lower returns.

### On The Time Junk Bonds Saved Capitalism

#### Michael Milken & High-Yield ("Junk") Bonds

In the 1980s, a guy named Michael Milken figured out something revolutionary: [if one offers people high enough returns, they will invest in almost anything](../references.qmd#milken-high-yield-bonds).

Wall Street called these "junk bonds" because they were trash. Milken called them "high-yield bonds" because marketing. He financed leveraged buyouts that the establishment said were impossible, raising billions.

The establishment said it would never work. It worked spectacularly until it didn't (Milken went to prison for unrelated fraud, which is how one knows it was successful).

**The Lesson:** To attract capital for high-risk ventures, one must offer absurdly high returns. VICTORY [Incentive Alignment Bonds](../appendix/incentive-alignment-bonds-paper-academic.qmd) promise 270% returns. This isn't generosity, it is economics. It is the "high-yield" premium necessary to compensate for betting on the unprecedented act of governments doing something smart.

If people invested in literal junk, they will invest in not dying. One just needs to price it correctly.

### On The Time George Soros Broke England

#### George Soros & The Quantum Fund

In 1992, [George Soros risked $10 billion betting that the UK would have to leave the European Exchange Rate Mechanism](../references.qmd#soros-bet-against-the-pound).

This was a binary political bet: Either the UK government capitulates, or Soros loses everything.

He won. Made over $1 billion in a single day. The Bank of England lost. The Queen was reportedly not amused.

**The Lesson:** It is possible to deploy immense private capital to bet on political outcomes. The trick is framing it as sophisticated arbitrage instead of what it really is: gambling on whether governments will do the obvious thing or the awful thing.

History suggests governments usually do the awful thing. But occasionally they surprise everyone. That is the bet this plan makes.

### On When Smart People Lost All Their Money (The Cautionary Tales)

**Long-Term Capital Management (LTCM): When Nobel Laureates Get Humbled**

In 1998, [a hedge fund run by actual Nobel Prize winners collapsed and required a $3.6 billion bailout](../references.qmd#long-term-capital-management-collapse).

Their crime? Building sophisticated mathematical models that accounted for everything except the part where Russia just... defaults. Whoops.

These were the smartest people in finance. They had Nobels. They had PhDs from MIT. They had models that predicted everything except reality.

**The Lesson:** Never underestimate systemic risk, also known as "the part where everything goes wrong at once."

For this project, the "black swan" is complete political failure. Everyone says no, the treaty dies, and the organizers look foolish.

This is why the plan includes:

- **Assurance contracts**: If the fundraising target isn't met, everyone gets their money back. No partial failures allowed.
- **First-loss philanthropic capital**: Wealthy altruists absorb the initial losses so regular investors don't get wiped out if things go sideways.

It is risk mitigation for people who understand that Nobel laureates can still be catastrophically wrong.

**The South Sea Bubble (1720): When Everyone Went Insane**

In 1720, [people in England went collectively mad and invested in a company that promised a monopoly on trade with South America](../references.qmd#south-sea-bubble-1720).

Neat! Except the company had almost no actual trade. And no profits. And no business plan beyond "tell people we're going to be really rich."

The stock went up 1,000%. Then it crashed. Everyone lost everything. Isaac Newton lost £20,000, which in today's money is "a lot." He famously said "I can calculate the motion of heavenly bodies, but not the madness of people."

**The Lesson:** Speculation based on hype alone ends badly.

This is why VICTORY Incentive Alignment Bond payouts are contractually tied to real, verifiable events:

- Treaty ratification (actual government signatures)
- Real government money flowing into the 1% Treaty Fund
- Actual treatments being tested in pragmatic clinical trials

No hype. No maybes. No "we are going to be really rich someday." Just math tied to observable reality.

If investors are going to lose their money, at least it won't be because the plan promised a monopoly on South American trade without checking if South America exists.

## 4. The Ultimate Failsafe: The Worst-Case Scenario is Still a Win

Even if one is skeptical of the above precedents, the core proposal has a powerful, built-in failsafe.

Imagine a decentralized institutes of health is a complete and total failure. Imagine every dollar of the {{< var treaty_annual_funding >}} is mismanaged, wasted, or simply dumped into the ocean.

The world would *still* be better off.

### Why?

Because society would still have achieved a **1% reduction in the global capacity for organized violence and destruction.**

- Fewer bombs.
- Fewer missiles.
- Fewer AI-powered weapons systems.

The absolute worst possible outcome of this plan is still a net gain for global security, stability, and human life. The best possible outcome is a cure for cancer, Alzheimer's, and every other disease that plagues humanity.

This asymmetrical risk profile, where failure is still a victory and success changes the course of human history, is the ultimate justification for the mission. It is a bet society can't afford not to take.
